Concentration Terms: Molarity, Molality, Mole Fraction, ppm
topics.nameHi: सांद्रता पद: मोलरता, मोललता, मोल अंश, ppm

keyConcepts: 1 Mole = 6.022 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro Number N_A).
Limiting Reagent is the reactant that is completely consumed first in a reaction and dictates the maximum amount of product formed.
Molality (m = moles of solute / kg of solvent) is INDEPENDENT of temperature, whereas Molarity (M = moles of solute / Volume of solution in L) depends on temperature.
Dilution Formula: M₁V₁ = M₂V₂; Mixing solutions: M_mix = (M₁V₁ + M₂V₂) / (V₁ + V₂).
formulaHints: Number of moles n = Weight (g) / Molar Mass = N / N_A = Volume at STP (L) / 22.4 L (or 22.7 L under standard IUPAC bar)
Empirical formula weight × n = Molecular formula weight
Molality from Molarity: m = 1000M / (1000d - M · M_solute)
commonMistakes: Dividing by mass of solution instead of mass of SOLVENT when calculating molality.
Identifying limiting reagent merely by smallest initial mass rather than dividing available moles by their stoichiometric coefficients.
shortTricks: Limiting Reagent Rule: Calculate (Moles / Stoichiometric Coefficient) for each reactant. The smallest value is strictly the limiting reagent.
For gas reactions at same T and P, volume ratio is directly the mole ratio (Gay-Lussac's Law).

topics.name: Aufbau Principle, Pauli's Exclusion Principle & Hund's Rule of Maximum Multiplicity
topics.nameHi: आउफबाऊ नियम, पाउली का अपवर्जन नियम, हुंड का नियम

keyConcepts: Four Quantum Numbers: Principal (n: shell/size), Azimuthal (l: subshell/shape, 0 to n-1), Magnetic (m_l: orientation, -l to +l), Spin (m_s: ±1/2).
Total nodes = n - 1; Radial nodes = n - l - 1; Angular nodes = l.
Aufbau Rule: Orbitals are filled in order of increasing (n + l). If (n + l) is same, lower n is filled first.
Anomalous electronic configurations due to half-filled and fully-filled extra stability: Cr (3d⁵ 4s¹) and Cu (3d¹⁰ 4s¹).
formulaHints: Bohr Radius: r_n = 0.529 n² / Z Å; Bohr Energy: E_n = -2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ (Z² / n²) J = -13.6 (Z² / n²) eV
Orbital angular momentum: L = √[l(l + 1)] · h / 2π
Spin-only magnetic moment: μ = √[n(n + 2)] BM (where n = number of unpaired electrons)
commonMistakes: Confusing radial nodes (n - l - 1) with angular nodes (l). For example, 3p orbital has n=3, l=1: Radial nodes = 3-1-1 = 1; Angular nodes = 1.
Writing electronic configuration of Cr as 3d⁴ 4s² instead of 3d⁵ 4s¹.
shortTricks: Maximum electrons in a shell = 2n²; Maximum electrons in a subshell = 2(2l + 1); Number of orbitals in a shell = n².
Degeneracy of hydrogen atom orbitals depends ONLY on principal quantum number n (e.g., 3s, 3p, 3d all have same energy in H-atom, degeneracy = n² = 9).

topics.nameHi: आयनन एन्थैल्पी की प्रवृत्तियां एवं अपवाद (Be > B, N > O)

topics.name: Electron Gain Enthalpy Trends (Cl > F, S > O) & Electronegativity (Pauling Scale)
topics.nameHi: इलेक्ट्रॉन लब्धि एन्थैल्पी (Cl > F, S > O) एवं विद्युतऋणात्मकता

keyConcepts: Isoelectronic Species: As positive charge increases, ionic radius decreases; as negative charge increases, radius increases (e.g., O²⁻ > F⁻ > Na⁺ > Mg²⁺ > Al³⁺).
Ionization Enthalpy Exception 1: Be (1s² 2s², fully filled) > B (1s² 2s² 2p¹); Exception 2: N (1s² 2s² 2p³, half filled) > O (1s² 2s² 2p⁴).
Electron Gain Enthalpy Exception: Chlorine has MORE negative electron gain enthalpy than Fluorine due to small size and high inter-electronic repulsion in 2p subshell of Fluorine (same for S > O).
formulaHints: Effective Nuclear Charge Z_eff = Z - σ (Slater's Rules)
Electronegativity order: F (4.0) > O (3.5) > N (3.0) ≈ Cl (3.0) > Br (2.8) > I (2.5) ≈ C (2.5) > H (2.1)
commonMistakes: Thinking Fluorine has the highest electron gain enthalpy. Fluorine has the highest ELECTRONEGATIVITY, but Chlorine has the highest ELECTRON GAIN ENTHALPY.
Predicting B > Be in 1st ionization enthalpy (Be is greater due to stable 2s² configuration and higher penetration of s-orbitals).
shortTricks: In isoelectronic series, radius ∝ 1 / Z (atomic number). Just look at atomic number: smaller Z = larger radius.
Noble gases have the largest atomic radius in their respective period because their radius is measured as Van der Waals radius.

topics.name: Hydrogen Bonding (Intermolecular vs Intramolecular)

keyConcepts: VSEPR Repulsion Order: Lone pair - Lone pair > Lone pair - Bond pair > Bond pair - Bond pair.
Steric Number = Number of bonded atoms + Lone pairs. Steric 2: linear; 3: trigonal planar; 4: tetrahedral; 5: trigonal bipyramidal; 6: octahedral.
Molecular Orbital Theory: For ≤ 14 electrons (e.g. N₂), σ2p_z is higher in energy than π2p_x, π2p_y. For > 14 electrons (e.g. O₂, F₂), σ2p_z is lower.
Bond Order = 0.5 × (N_b - N_a). If Bond Order > 0, molecule exists. Higher bond order = shorter bond length, higher bond dissociation energy.
O₂ is PARAMAGNETIC with 2 unpaired electrons in π*2p antibonding orbitals.
formulaHints: Steric Number SN = 0.5 [V + M - C + A] (V = valence electrons of central atom, M = monovalent surrounding atoms, C = cation charge, A = anion charge)
Dipole moment μ = q × d (1 Debye = 3.33564 × 10⁻³⁰ C·m)
Bond order trick for diatomics (14 e⁻ = 3.0, each 1 e⁻ step away reduces bond order by 0.5)
commonMistakes: Calling shape of XeF₄ tetrahedral (Steric number 6 with 2 lone pairs = Square Planar).
Calling NF₃ more polar than NH₃. NH₃ has much higher dipole moment (1.47 D) because lone pair and N-H bond dipoles reinforce each other, whereas in NF₃ they oppose.
shortTricks: Bond order memory scale: 14 e⁻ (N₂) = 3.0; 13 or 15 e⁻ (N₂⁺, O₂⁺) = 2.5; 12 or 16 e⁻ (C₂, O₂) = 2.0; 11 or 17 e⁻ = 1.5; 10 or 18 e⁻ = 1.0.
Any species with odd electrons or fractional bond order is GUARANTEED to be paramagnetic.

topics.name: Gibbs Free Energy (ΔG = ΔH - TΔS) & Spontaneity Criteria, ΔG° = -RT ln K

keyConcepts: IUPAC sign convention: Work done ON system is positive (+w), work done BY system is negative (-w). Heat absorbed is positive (+q), heat released is negative (-q).
Spontaneity: For spontaneous process at constant T and P, ΔG < 0. At equilibrium, ΔG = 0.
If ΔH < 0 and ΔS > 0: Spontaneous at ALL temperatures.
If ΔH > 0 and ΔS < 0: Non-spontaneous at ALL temperatures.
formulaHints: ΔH = ΔU + Δn_g RT (where Δn_g = moles of gaseous products - moles of gaseous reactants)
ΔG° = -2.303 RT log₁₀ K_eq
Standard enthalpy of formation Δ_f H° of pure elements in standard state is ZERO (e.g. O₂(g), C(graphite), Br₂(l), I₂(s))
commonMistakes: Assuming C(diamond) has Δ_f H° = 0. Graphite is the thermodynamic reference state of carbon, so Δ_f H°(graphite) = 0, but Δ_f H°(diamond) = 1.9 kJ/mol.
Forgetting to convert ΔH from kJ to J when using ΔG = ΔH - TΔS (since ΔS is usually given in J/K·mol).
shortTricks: Temperature at which a reaction becomes spontaneous (cross-over temperature): T = ΔH / ΔS.
Free expansion of ideal gas into vacuum (P_ext = 0) in insulated container: w = 0, q = 0, ΔU = 0, ΔT = 0.

topics.name: Solubility Product (K_sp) & Common Ion Effect in Precipitation

keyConcepts: Le Chatelier's Principle: Adding inert gas at CONSTANT VOLUME causes NO SHIFT in equilibrium. Adding inert gas at CONSTANT PRESSURE shifts toward the side with more gaseous moles.
Endothermic reactions: K increases as Temperature increases. Exothermic reactions: K decreases as Temperature increases.
Buffer Solution: Acidic Buffer (Weak Acid + Conjugate Base salt, e.g. CH₃COOH + CH₃COONa): pH = pK_a + log([Salt]/[Acid]).
Condition for precipitation: Ionic Product Q_sp > K_sp.
formulaHints: pH = -log₁₀[H⁺]; pH + pOH = 14 (at 25°C, where K_w = 10⁻¹⁴)
Weak acid pH = 0.5 (pK_a - log C); [H⁺] = √(K_a · C)
Salt of Weak Acid + Strong Base: pH = 7 + 0.5(pK_a + log C)
Salt of Strong Acid + Weak Base: pH = 7 - 0.5(pK_b + log C)
Salt of Weak Acid + Weak Base: pH = 7 + 0.5(pK_a - pK_b)
commonMistakes: Calculating pH of 10⁻⁸ M HCl as 8.0. An acidic solution can NEVER have pH > 7! Must include water dissociation: [H⁺]_total = 10⁻⁸ + 10⁻⁷ = 1.1 × 10⁻⁷ M → pH ≈ 6.96.
Changing K_c or K_p when concentration or pressure changes. Equilibrium constant K changes ONLY with Temperature.
shortTricks: For salt A_x B_y dissolving to give s solubility: K_sp = x^x · y^y · s^(x+y). For AB (e.g. AgCl): K_sp = s²; For AB₂ (e.g. CaF₂): K_sp = 4s³; For AB₃: K_sp = 27s⁴; For A₂B₃: K_sp = 108s⁵.

topics.name: Purification Techniques: Chromatography & Qualitative/Quantitative Analysis (Dumas, Kjeldahl)

nmcNotes: Chromatography and detection of elements (Lassaigne test) and estimation of N, halogens, S, P are core practical organic topics tested vigorously.
keyConcepts: Carbocation Stability: 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃⁺ (stabilized by +M, Hyperconjugation, +I).
Carbanion Stability: CH₃⁻ > 1° > 2° > 3° (stabilized by -M, -I, higher s-character: sp > sp² > sp³).
Acidity of Carboxylic Acids / Phenols: Enhanced by electron-withdrawing groups (-M, -I), decreased by electron-donating groups (+M, +I).
Ortho effect in benzoic acids makes substituted ortho-benzoic acids always stronger than benzoic acid regardless of nature of substituent.
formulaHints: Kjeldahl's Nitrogen % = (1.4 × N × V) / Mass of organic compound
Dumas Nitrogen % = (28 / 22400) × (V_N2 at STP / W) × 100%
Carius Halogen % = (Atomic weight of X / Molecular weight of AgX) × (Mass of AgX / W) × 100%
commonMistakes: Applying Kjeldahl's method to nitro (-NO₂), azo (-N=N-), or nitrogen in pyridine ring (Kjeldahl method FAILS for these because nitrogen is not converted to ammonium sulfate).
Confusing mesomeric (+M) with inductive (-I) for halogens attached to benzene ring (Halogens are deactivating due to strong -I, but ortho/para directing due to +M).
shortTricks: Acidic Strength Trick: Strong acid has stable conjugate base. Check conjugate base stability: Anion on more electronegative atom, resonance dispersal, -M > -H > -I.
Basic Strength in aqueous solution of aliphatic amines: For ethyl group: 2° > 3° > 1° > NH₃ (213); For methyl group: 2° > 1° > 3° > NH₃ (213 rule).

topics.name: Alkanes: Free Radical Halogenation Mechanism, Wurtz Reaction, Decarboxylation
topics.nameHi: ऐल्केन: मुक्त मूलक हैलोजनीकरण, वुर्ट्ज अभिक्रिया

topics.name: Conformations of Ethane and Butane (Sawhorse and Newman Projections)

Ozonolysis of Alkenes & Alkynes (Reductive vs Oxidative)

topics.nameHi: ऐरोमैटिक हाइड्रोकार्बन: हकल नियम, इलेक्ट्रॉनरागी प्रतिस्थापन

keyConcepts: Wurtz Reaction: 2 R-X + 2 Na (dry ether) → R-R + 2 NaX (good only for symmetrical alkanes with even number of carbons).
Markovnikov's Rule: In electrophilic addition to unsymmetrical alkene, positive part (H⁺) attaches to carbon with MORE hydrogen atoms.
Peroxide / Kharasch Effect: Anti-Markovnikov addition occurs ONLY with HBr in presence of peroxide (NOT with HCl or HI because one step is endothermic).
Ozonolysis: Double bond is cleanly cleaved; C=C becomes two C=O groups. Reductive (Zn/H₂O) gives aldehydes/ketones; Oxidative (H₂O₂/KMnO₄) oxidizes aldehydes to acids.
Huckel's Rule: Planar cyclic fully-conjugated rings with (4n + 2) π electrons are aromatic.
formulaHints: Staggered conformation of ethane is more stable than eclipsed by ~12.5 kJ/mol due to minimal torsional strain.
Anti conformation of n-butane is the most stable conformer (dihedral angle 180°).
commonMistakes: Applying peroxide effect to HCl or HI (Peroxide effect is strictly observed ONLY for HBr!).
Forgetting that terminal alkynes (e.g. propyne, ethyne) react with Tollens' reagent and ammoniacal cuprous chloride, but non-terminal alkynes (but-2-yne) do not.
shortTricks: Ozonolysis Trick: Just erase the C=C double bond and stick an oxygen atom (=O) on both ends of the cleaved fragments.
Electrophilic aromatic substitution: -OH, -NH₂, -CH₃ are ortho/para activating; -NO₂, -CHO, -COOH, -SO₃H are meta deactivating.

topics.name: Abnormal Molar Mass & Van 't Hoff Factor (i): Association and Dissociation
topics.nameHi: असामान्य आण्विक द्रव्यमान एवं वान्ट हॉफ गुणक (i)

keyConcepts: Positive Deviation from Raoult's Law: A-B interaction is weaker than A-A and B-B; ΔH_mix > 0, ΔV_mix > 0, vapor pressure higher than ideal (e.g. Ethanol + Acetone).
Negative Deviation: A-B interaction is stronger than A-A and B-B; ΔH_mix < 0, ΔV_mix < 0, vapor pressure lower (e.g. Chloroform + Acetone due to H-bonding).
Osmotic Pressure π = i C R T is the preferred colligative property for determining molar mass of biomolecules (proteins, polymers) because it is measurable at room temperature.
Van 't Hoff Factor: Dissociation i = 1 + (n - 1)α; Association i = 1 + (1/n - 1)α.
formulaHints: Relative Lowering of Vapor Pressure: (P° - P_s) / P° = i · x_solute = i (n / (n + N))
Elevation in Boiling Point: ΔT_b = i · K_b · m
Depression in Freezing Point: ΔT_f = i · K_f · m
Osmotic Pressure: π = i · (n/V) · R T
commonMistakes: Forgetting Van 't Hoff factor i when calculating colligative properties for ionic solutes like NaCl (i=2), CaCl₂ (i=3), Al₂(SO₄)₃ (i=5).
Confusing units of R in osmotic pressure: If P is in atm and V in liters, R = 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K.
shortTricks: Highest boiling point or highest osmotic pressure in equal molarity solutions belongs to the solute with HIGHEST (i × C). Lowest freezing point also belongs to highest (i × C).
Chloroform + Acetone forms a maximum boiling azeotrope because it shows negative deviation.

topics.name: Galvanic Cells, Standard Electrode Potential & Electrochemical Series
Nernst Equation & Applications to Cell EMF and Equilibrium Constant

Conductance, Specific Conductivity (κ), Molar Conductivity (Λ_m)

topics.nameHi: विद्युत अपघटन एवं फैराडे के नियम

keyConcepts: E°_cell = E°_cathode - E°_anode (using standard REDUCTION potentials).
Reaction is spontaneous if E°_cell > 0 (which means ΔG° < 0).
Conductivity (κ) DECREASES with dilution because number of ions per unit volume decreases.
Molar conductivity (Λ_m) INCREASES with dilution for both strong and weak electrolytes (reaches maximum Λ°_m at infinite dilution).
Faraday's 1st Law: m = (Equivalent Weight / 96500) × I × t.
formulaHints: Nernst Equation at 298 K: E_cell = E°_cell - (0.0591 / n) log₁₀ Q
log₁₀ K_c = n E°_cell / 0.0591
Molar conductivity: Λ_m = 1000 κ / M (in S·cm²·mol⁻¹ when κ is in S·cm⁻¹)
Degree of dissociation of weak electrolyte: α = Λ_m / Λ°_m
commonMistakes: Multiplying electrode potential E° by stoichiometric coefficients when balancing reaction. E° is an INTENSIVE property and NEVER multiplies with stoichiometric coefficients!
Confusing anode and cathode polarities: In Galvanic cell, Anode is Negative, Cathode is Positive (remember ANOX - Anode Oxidation). In Electrolytic cell, Anode is connected to Positive terminal.
shortTricks: 1 Faraday of charge (96,500 C) deposits 1 gram-equivalent of any substance at the electrode.
Charge required to reduce 1 mole of MnO₄⁻ to Mn²⁺ is 5 Faraday (change in oxidation state is +7 to +2 = 5).

Collision Theory of Chemical Reactions & Activation Energy

keyConcepts: Order can be zero, fractional, or negative, and is determined EXPERIMENTALLY. Molecularity is always a positive integer (1, 2, 3) and applies only to elementary steps.
First Order Reaction: Integrated rate law k = (2.303 / t) log₁₀(a / (a - x)); Half-life t_1/2 = 0.693 / k is completely INDEPENDENT of initial concentration.
Zero Order Reaction: Integrated rate law k = (x / t); Half-life t_1/2 = a / (2k) is directly proportional to initial concentration.
Catalyst increases rate of reaction by providing an alternative pathway with LOWER activation energy, without altering ΔH or equilibrium constant K.
formulaHints: Units of rate constant k = (mol/L)^(1 - n) · s⁻¹ (where n = order)
Arrhenius two-temperature formula: log₁₀(k₂ / k₁) = (E_a / 2.303 R) · [(T₂ - T₁) / (T₁ T₂)]
First order time relationships: t_75% = 2 × t_50%; t_87.5% = 3 × t_50%; t_99.9% ≈ 10 × t_50%
commonMistakes: Confusing units of k for different orders: Zero order has units mol·L⁻¹·s⁻¹; First order s⁻¹; Second order L·mol⁻¹·s⁻¹.
Thinking catalyst shifts the equilibrium position. Catalyst only helps equilibrium to be attained FASTER.
shortTricks: In first order reaction, time required for 99% completion is twice the time required for 90% completion: t_99% = 2 × t_90%.
Plot of ln k versus 1/T yields a straight line with slope = -E_a / R and intercept = ln A.

keyConcepts: Lanthanoid Contraction: Steady decrease in atomic and ionic radii of lanthanoids due to poor shielding of 4f electrons. Consequence: 4d and 5d series have nearly identical radii (Zr ≈ Hf, Nb ≈ Ta).
Highest oxidation state in 3d series is +7 shown by Manganese in KMnO₄; Osmium shows +8 in OsO₄.
K₂Cr₂O₇ in acidic medium acts as strong oxidizing agent: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O (n-factor = 6).
KMnO₄: n-factor in acidic medium = 5 (MnO₄⁻ → Mn²⁺); in neutral/weakly alkaline medium = 3 (MnO₄⁻ → MnO₂); in strongly basic medium = 1 (MnO₄⁻ → MnO₄²⁻).
formulaHints: Spin-only magnetic moment μ = √[n(n + 2)] BM
Lanthanoid most common and stable oxidation state = +3; Ce shows +4 (strong oxidant), Eu shows +2 (strong reductant)
commonMistakes: Confusing color origin in KMnO₄ and K₂Cr₂O₇: They are colored due to CHARGE TRANSFER spectra (ligand to metal charge transfer LMCT), NOT d-d transition (because Mn⁷⁺ and Cr⁶⁺ have d⁰ configuration!).
Thinking actinoids have fewer oxidation states than lanthanoids (actinoids exhibit wider range of oxidation states due to comparable energies of 5f, 6d, and 7s).
shortTricks: KMnO₄ n-factor mnemonic: BAN 153 (Basic = 1, Acidic = 5, Neutral = 3).
Chromyl Chloride Test confirms chloride presence: forms deep red fumes of CrO₂Cl₂ which turn NaOH yellow (Na₂CrO₄).

topics.nameHi: क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत (CFT): अष्टफलकीय व चतुष्फलकीय विपाटन

keyConcepts: Ambidentate Ligands: Ligands having two donor atoms but binding through only one at a time (e.g. NO₂⁻ vs ONO⁻, SCN⁻ vs NCS⁻), giving rise to LINKAGE isomerism.
Chelate Effect: Complexes with multidentate chelating ligands (e.g. EDTA⁴⁻, en) are significantly more stable than complexes with monodentate ligands due to positive entropy change (ΔS > 0).
CFT Octahedral Splitting: d-orbitals split into lower t_2g (d_xy, d_yz, d_xz) and higher e_g (d_x²-y², d_z²); Δ_o.
Tetrahedral Splitting: Δ_t = (4/9) Δ_o; Pairing energy P is always greater than Δ_t, so tetrahedral complexes are ALWAYS high spin.
Spectrochemical Series: I⁻ < Br⁻ < S²⁻ < SCN⁻ < Cl⁻ < F⁻ < OH⁻ < C₂O₄²⁻ < H₂O < NCS⁻ < EDTA⁴⁻ < NH₃ < en < CN⁻ < CO (Strong field ligands cause pairing).
formulaHints: CFSE for octahedral: [-0.4 × n(t_2g) + 0.6 × n(e_g)] Δ_o + m·P
Number of ions produced in solution: [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃ gives 4 ions (1 complex cation + 3 chloride anions), precipitates 3 moles of AgCl with AgNO₃.
commonMistakes: Naming anionic complexes with standard metal name instead of '-ate' ending (e.g. ferrate, cuprate, cobaltate).
Assuming tetrahedral complexes show geometrical isomerism (Tetrahedral complexes NEVER show cis-trans isomerism because all positions are adjacent/equivalent).
shortTricks: Carbonyls: Carbon monoxide (CO) is the strongest field ligand; back bonding from filled metal d-orbital to empty π* antibonding orbital of CO strengthens M-C bond and weakens C-O bond.
[Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ has Co³⁺ (d⁶) with NH₃ acting as strong field ligand → all electrons paired in t_2g⁶ → diamagnetic, low spin, d²sp³.

topics.name: Reactions due to α-Hydrogen: Aldol Condensation, Cross Aldol Condensation, Cannizzaro Reaction
Carboxylic Acids: Acidity, Decarboxylation (Kolbe Electrolysis, Soda-lime) & Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) Reaction

keyConcepts: Reactivity towards nucleophilic addition: Aldehydes > Ketones (due to less steric hindrance and smaller +I effect of alkyl groups); HCHO > CH₃CHO > CH₃COCH₃.
Iodoform Test (Yellow precipitate of CHI₃): Given by compounds having CH₃-C=O group or CH₃-CH(OH)- group (e.g., ethanol, acetaldehyde, acetone, 2-pentanone).
Aldol Condensation: Requires AT LEAST ONE α-hydrogen atom in presence of dilute base (dil. NaOH).
Cannizzaro Reaction: Undergone by aldehydes LACKING α-hydrogen (HCHO, Benzaldehyde) in concentrated alkali (50% NaOH), disproportionating into an alcohol and a carboxylate salt.
formulaHints: Rosenmund Reduction: R-COCl + H₂ (Pd/BaSO₄, quinoline) → R-CHO
HVZ Reaction: R-CH₂-COOH + X₂ / Red P → R-CH(X)-COOH (α-halogenation)
Tollens' reagent: Ammoniacal silver nitrate [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺; Fehling's solution: Alkaline Cu²⁺ tartrate (aromatic aldehydes do NOT reduce Fehling's solution!)
commonMistakes: Thinking Benzaldehyde reduces Fehling's solution. Benzaldehyde reduces Tollens' reagent but FAILS to reduce Fehling's solution!
Forgetting that Formic Acid (HCOOH) gives positive Tollens' and Fehling's test because it contains both an aldehyde group and a carboxylic acid group.
shortTricks: Cannizzaro Disproportionation mnemonic: 'Self-redox when NO alpha-H': 1 molecule oxidizes to acid salt, 1 molecule reduces to alcohol.
Cross Cannizzaro with Formaldehyde: Formaldehyde is ALWAYS oxidized to formate (HCOO⁻) because nucleophilic attack of OH⁻ is fastest on HCHO.

keyConcepts: Sucrose is a NON-REDUCING sugar because reducing groups of both glucose (C1) and fructose (C2) are involved in glycosidic linkage (α-D-glucose C1 to β-D-fructose C2).
Maltose (two α-D-glucose, α-1,4-linkage) and Lactose (β-D-galactose C1 to β-D-glucose C4) are REDUCING sugars.
All naturally occurring amino acids are L-amino acids (except Glycine which is optically inactive because it has no chiral carbon).
Protein Denaturation: Secondary and tertiary structures are destroyed by heat or pH changes, but PRIMARY structure (peptide bonds) remains completely intact.
Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K; Water-soluble vitamins: B-complex and C (cannot be stored in body, must be supplied regularly in diet).
formulaHints: Invert sugar: Hydrolysis of dextrorotatory sucrose (+66.5°) produces mixture of D-(+)-glucose (+52.5°) and D-(-)-fructose (-92.4°), resulting in net levorotatory mixture (-39.9°).
DNA bases: Adenine (A), Guanine (G), Cytosine (C), Thymine (T); RNA replaces Thymine with Uracil (U).
commonMistakes: Thinking fructose is an aldose. Fructose is a KETOHEXOSE, yet it reduces Tollens' and Fehling's solutions due to Lobry de Bruyn-Alberda van Ekenstein keto-enol tautomerism in alkaline medium!
Confusing Nucleoside with Nucleotide: Nucleoside = Base + Sugar; Nucleotide = Base + Sugar + Phosphate group.
shortTricks: Essential amino acids mnemonic: PVT TIM HALL (Phenylalanine, Valine, Threonine, Tryptophan, Isoleucine, Methionine, Histidine, Arginine, Leucine, Lysine).
Base pairing rule (Chargaff): In DNA, A pairs with T via 2 hydrogen bonds (A=T); G pairs with C via 3 hydrogen bonds (G≡C).
